title: Tenali Raman and the Miserly Confectioner's Scale

full_text:
In the food bazaar of Vijayanagara, a notoriously dishonest sweetmaker named Mithai Ram operated a thriving shop. He was famous for using two sets of brass weights: a lighter, hollowed-out set when selling sweets, and a heavier set when buying raw sugar, cheating poor customers on every transaction.
When poor mothers complained that their bag of laddus felt unusually light, Mithai Ram would sneer:
'My scales are blessed by the goddess of fortune! If the sweets feel light, it is because my sugar is as airy and delicate as celestial clouds!'

Tenali Raman decided to cure the dishonest merchant.

Tenali went to his friend, a skilled coppersmith, and had ten special coins crafted:
They were brass coins cast with a thin gold-gilded foil surface, but hollow inside, filled with light elder-pith, so that while they looked identical to heavy gold dinars, each coin weighed barely a fraction of a feather!

Tenali walked into Mithai Ram’s shop:
'Master Mithai Ram, I desire to purchase ten pounds of your finest saffron almond halwa for a royal banquet.'

Mithai Ram’s eyes gleamed with greed. He used his hollowed-out, fraudulent weights, scooped out barely seven pounds of halwa, packed it into a box, and placed it upon the scale:
'Ten pounds exactly, Master Tenali! That will be ten gold dinars!'

Tenali nodded with a pleasant smile.
He reached into his purse and counted out the ten hollow, lightweight gold coins, placing them in Mithai Ram’s palm.

Mithai Ram lifted the coins: they felt unnaturally light, like dry husks!
Mithai Ram shouted in outrage:
'Tenali! What trickery is this? These gold coins are completely hollow and weightless! They are not worth five coppers!'

Tenali Raman looked at him with innocent, wide eyes:
'Why, Master Mithai Ram! Did you not proclaim just moments ago that your sweets feel light because your sugar is as airy and delicate as celestial clouds?
My gold coins were forged in the exact same celestial cloud!
They are delicate, airy, spiritual coins!
A light box of halwa deserves a light purse of gold!
When your scale becomes honest, my coins will regain their weight!'

The surrounding crowd of customers burst into deafening cheers and laughter!
Mithai Ram turned crimson with shame, realizing that his own excuse had been turned into a weapon against him.
He fell to his knees, smashed his fraudulent weights with an iron hammer before the crowd, and swore to use only certified imperial balances henceforth.
Tenali smiled, paid him with real silver for the actual weight, and distributed the halwa to the poor children of the bazaar.
moral: Cheating the public with hollow weights invites a sharp-witted customer who pays with hollow coins.
